quote_text: 1987 world cup Pakistan Vs West indies Pakistan is down to its last wicket with two runs required in one ball. The west Indian baller Courtney Walsh comes running into ball and Jaffar on the non-striker's end leaves the crease early. Walsh anticipating this, stops. some of you may know  what happens next some of you may not but today's story is not about that, Today's story is about the journey that brought us here. It's about the tremendous psychological pressure on a 25 year old. It's about a split-second decision that changed the course of a world cup, and most importantly, it's about a single man's regret. Our story begins from the first time West indies face Pakistan in a world cup. It was the first world cup to be ever played 1975. Coming into the world cup both these teams were being treated as unpredictables. No one could imagine the behemoth that west indies were soon to become. and shockingly that juggernaut could have been stopped right at the start. that too by Pakistan. Chasing a total of 267 West indies had been demolished by the Pakistani bowling. reduced to 20349 that 64 runs required with only one wicket in hand with a keeper and a baller at the grease. The match was done but then cricket happened, the bowling that had dismantled the greatest batsman of this generation couldn't dislodge two tail enders from the crees for 16 overs Derek Murray and Andy Roberts stood side by side, defending against the Pakistani attack and finally winning the match with two balls to spare and so began the rise of West Indian cricket not a smooth sailing but a struggle amidst adversity and grit The importance of that grit could be seen at the end of the group stage, when the knocked out Pakistan  had a higher net run rate than both the qualifying teams. If Pakistan had won that match West indies would have been the one to be knocked out. Murray and Roberts had nearly single-handedly saved West Indian hegemony. and 13-year-old Courtney Walsh had seen this miracle happen, in a small TV in his hometown Jamaica. The teenager had seen two of his countrymen honored, celebrated and adored as heroes and so the first seeds were sown. The young boy would see the finals of two more world cups. One won and one lost, each of which would harden his resolve to play for his country. A resolve that would be rewarded in 1984. He had been given a spot in the West Indian team. Now do understand here, getting into the West Indian team at that time, meant competing for a spot with the fearsome foursome of west Indian cricket. but the youngster with his cool as eyes gentlemanly persona yet having the ability to knock off a batsman's head, if required not only did he stand tall but he earned his way into the team for the 1987 world cup. This was the culmination of his dreams. His time to prove himself and finally by his own hands, make true his destiny…. And in the first match he played in the world cup….. with the chance to win the match for his country. He failed & Quite miserably at that… England, while chasing a target 243, had been reduced to a 131 for 6. Allan Lamb had somehow steadied the inning but England needed 91 runs in the last 10 overs to win. A near impossibility at that time. But an impossibility that started becoming possible, slowly and gradually the target was been brought down, and by the time Walsh was introduced into the attack, England needed 35 runs in 3 overs…. A towering task still.. But then Walsh went for 31 runs in 2 overs That by itself could be understood. May be he just had a bad day. But what made this humiliating… was the way in which it happened. 13 runs required of the last over. Lamb hits 2 and 4 in the first 2 balls.. The next ball, goes for a leg side wides 4. Next – A no ball with a single run taken. And finally the last ball. A full toss. That was hit across the boundary… Walsh had failed in a disgraceful manner. The psychological burden that such a lost places on a 25 year old…. It’s stuff of anyone’s nightmare. But, the world cup wasn’t done. The youngster had to go on. Especially with all the teams easily defeating Sri lanka, The next match could decide the outcome of the group stage. And the next match, against the tournament favorites Pakistan in Lahore. The champions were to face their challengers. In practically an elimination match. So no doubt, all eyes were glued to to the TV, and all ears to radios, At the start of what was to be a wild see-sawing match. West Indies got off to an amazing start but a 2 wicket spell from Jaffer turned the tides. West Indian captain Viv Richards then pulled ahead, by hitting a 51 ball century. But then the opposing team captain Imran Khan took him out, and then went on to remove most of the West Indian team. By the time the dust settled, West indies had somehow gone from 169 for 4 to 216 all out. A meltdown of epic proportions… And seeing this, Pakistan seemingly went,”Ya will do you won better”. They got reduced to 110 for 5. I told you, "It was a seesaw imagined I". Now it looks some furious batting from wicketkeeper Saleem Yusuf to dig them out of this hole. With West Indies also seeming to want to help the wicketkeeper. or else why would they drop him 3 times? 3 times….on the way to his half century. So, with West Indians backing him up, Saleem looked ready to bring the match home… When in the 47th over, Just 15 runs away from the target Courtney Walsh took him out. The pressure from last match, which could make any grown man crumble, that seemed to have turn him into a sharp diamond. A sharpness that had nearly singlehandedly cut through, the entire Pakistani middle order. The disgraced youngster had brought his team back into the game. Then, with the 48th over of Patterson going for just 2 runs and 2 wickets. Pakistan was down to its last wicket, with 14 runs required in the last over and just two tail enders on the pitch The match seemed just about wrapped up. And then in a move that even seemed to shock even his own team Viv Richards handed the ball to the young Walsh. Walsh was the reason West indies were floundering in this world cup. & now to be made responsible for keeping them in the tournament. Nobody would have blamed him. if simply he refused. Asking somebody else to take over. But Courtney Walsh simply took the ball, and went to his starting lineup. What was pressure to others, to him was a golden opportunity to him to redeem himself. There was no way he was going to let this go. So, as he got ready to ball, He saw Abdul Qadir facing him. Now Qadir could be described as an antithesis to Walsh. Wherein Walsh was the gentlemanly pace bowler. Qadir was the spin bowler with the temperament of a fiery pacer. Easy to anger and then letting emotions fuel his performance… Today standing in front of his home crowd, He looked just about ready to destroy his opposition. And so, started the dual. The first ball was hit to long on, with the expectation of taking 2. But seeing the fielder run in, Qadir stooped jaffar from returning. With Qadir off strike, the plan was simple, to keep Jaffer batting, but somehow, he hit an inside-out slog & Qadir was back on strike And this is where the script started going wrong. The next ball was supposed to be a single. But Walsh failed to cover it properly. And Qudir took two runs. Still it wasn’t a big deal. Walsh had balled really well till this point & all he had to do was continue to box out Qadir. Make sure that doesn’t hit any big shots, And as if jinxing himself, he did just that. The ball was pitched up, Qadir moved to his leg-side, and hit the ball as hard as he could. Walsh stood in stunned silence. As he saw the ball, sail across the boundary. It was a six. The target was down to 4 runs in 2 balls. The game had turned, the pressure was back on The youngster had once again taken a winning situation. And turned it on its head. He was about to fail his country again. How many times, does a coincidence have to repeat. for it to be pattern. How many times should he crumble under pressure before he realizes… he is a failure? The thoughts that must have gone through Walsh's head at that time, They were nothing short of self-torture. And yet, he just smiled. And then  got back to his starting point. The match was not over yet. He had not failed yet. The next ball, a yorker, that was just a bit high. hit to deep extra cover and 2 runs taken. 2 required of 1 ball. Now standing at the brink of defeat, Walsh still looked unfazed. He took the ball, started walking back. & thought of something very peculiar. Last ball, when Qadir had hit the ball, Jaffar was nearly halfway down the pitch. So as he started his run up, he kept one eye on Jaffar, with absolutely no intention of actually balling the ball, Last ball had shown, they would run, no matter where the ball went. And with the field brought in for the last ball That start that Jaffar was getting. May become the difference between a win and a loss & so as Walsh approached the crease, & Jaffar started running. Walsh simply stopped. As you can see here, Jaffar was still being carried away by the momentum He had no hope of ever getting back on time. So, Walsh had a choice to make. Either take off the bails and end the match right now. or let him go. Running a batsman out like this though frowned upon, was well within the rules. People may crib but his nation would understand. At least for his own country, he would be a hero. Just like Murray, just like Roberts. Logic, emotions and even good sense dictated, that he should have done what needed to be done. And then, he did this. Standing there, with his arms crossed, not moving a single muscle. He simply looked on. He would win on his own terms. Or he would face the consequences. After all, a win that doesn’t fit in with your soul. What use is such victory? And so he walked away to his starting point. Ready to ball the final ball. A ball that would decide, their win or loss. A ball that would decide, how he was remembered henceforth… And a ball which was then sliced away, for a boundary. By the time the group stages were done, what was predicted earlier, turned into a fact West Indies on third place still had the highest run rate in the group. If West indies had won the match, they would have been first and Pakistan would have been out. but, the fact remained. West Indies was knowcked out. And though afterwards, Walsh had been gifted, an exotic carpet as a thanks from the Pakistani president Zia ul haq Though afterwards, he was lauded by the world media for his sportsmanship. And though he then went on to play for a 17 more years, becoming a legend for his spirit and grit. And finally though Walsh’s actions, till date are listed in the annals of the greatest moments in world cup history. One question naturally arises, doesn’t it? Does he regret it? After not winning a single world cup in his career. Does he regret it ?? The thing is the answer to this question was provided by Walsh himself, in another world cup. When playing in the 1992 world cup, with West Indies in a must win match against Australia, & Walsh balling the last over. He once again, Ran in, Stopped & Refused to run out Stuart law. The Gentleman had spoken through his actions. No words were ever needed…. Thank you for watching this video!!! I hope you enjoyed it!! and I hope you have a good day!! thank you!!!
